tldr: Brent/WTI crashed 11.4%/7.5% Monday ($104.23/$96.26) on Iran's signaled 2-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, erasing October's entire war premium -- but Trump/Netanyahu still keep strikes 'on the table' post-midterms, so don't treat this as resolved.

A hot October ISM Manufacturing print (55.5 vs 54.5 consensus) swung Fed-funds pricing toward a ~75% probability of a December HIKE, not a cut -- a genuine headwind for duration and growth equities (XLK/SMH took the largest downward call revisions).

Gold (+1.65%), silver (+2.17%) and GDX (+2.67%) rallied Monday on falling yields/a weaker dollar even as hike odds rose -- a safe-haven decoupling for the levered silver book, not confirmation of a clean new uptrend.

Hyperscaler credit stress hit fresh records (Oracle 5Y CDS >220bp, Meta 114.79bp) after Meta's first negative FCF since 2012 -- the AI-capex overhang behind Monday's HK-tech bounce (Tencent +2.2%, Xiaomi +6.1%) remains unresolved.

Correction: China's rare-earth truce runs to Jan 10 2027, not Nov 10 as previously flagged -- the real flashpoint is the Jan 1 Pentagon-supplier ban colliding with the Jan 10 truce expiry, a 9-day window, not next week.
US midterm elections today; VIX jumped 8.91% to 21.15 on election/RBA-hike hedging even as the S&P fell only 0.51% -- options markets are pricing more fear than the cash tape shows.

regime.label: Hawkish ISM/Fed-Hike Repricing Collides With Record AI-Credit Stress as the Hormuz War-Premium Unwinds
regime.oneLiner: Monday's oil-premium collapse is a genuine relief valve, but a hot ISM print pushing Fed-funds pricing toward a December hike and record hyperscaler credit stress keep the broader risk backdrop fragile into today's elections and RBA decision.

topNews.headline: Brent crashes 11.4% to $104.23, WTI -7.55% to $96.26 as Iran-Qatar talks raise Hormuz reopening hopes
topNews.actionable: The Hormuz-risk premium underpinning XLE and the commodities sleeve is unwinding fast on diplomacy, not resolution -- treat today's drop as reversible, not a new regime.

topNews.headline: Gold rallies to ~$3,955-3,966 (+1.85%), silver to ~$50.7-50.8 (+3.6%) on dollar weakness as 10-yr yield hits 7-week low
topNews.actionable: Constructive for the GDX/SILJ/SLVP book, but the move runs counter to the Fed's still-live December-hike bias -- don't assume it's the start of a clean new leg higher.

topNews.headline: Fed holds at 3.75-4.00%, Warsh gives no explicit December signal; hike odds near 76-85% into the Dec 8-9 meeting
topNews.actionable: Keep duration exposure neutral and don't extrapolate Monday's metals bid into a dovish-Fed thesis.

topNews.headline: HK tech bounces hard: Tencent +2.2%, Xiaomi +6.1%, Hang Seng TECH +2.85%
topNews.actionable: A one-day bounce worth noting for the 0700/0981/1810 basket, but not yet confirmation the AI-capex credibility overhang has cleared.

topNews.headline: Correction: China's rare-earth truce runs to Jan 10, 2027, not Nov 10 -- but a new Jan 1 Pentagon-supplier ban creates a 9-day collision
topNews.actionable: There is no Nov 10 cliff for the MP/LYC.AX/UUUU watchlist -- the next real catalyst window is the Jan 1/Jan 10 turn-of-year collision, not next week.

signals: Watch SHY (short-duration Treasuries): pUp3m 0.65 at 0.55 confidence -- front-end carry stays attractive as Fed-funds pricing swings toward a ~75% probability of a December hike.

Watch XLE/USO: Monday's oil-premium unwind is explicitly two-sided (Doha talks ended 'without a breakthrough'), so a stalled Iran negotiation post-midterms could reverse much of the crash -- confidence ~0.48-0.50, not a clean directional call either way.

Watch GLD/SLV: Monday's rally is a safe-haven decoupling (hike odds rose at the same time), not a rates-driven move -- consider the metals/miners sleeve's resilience to the next Fed-pricing shift as the real test.

Rare-earth basket (MP/LYC.AX/UUUU/USAR): the near-term Nov 9/10 deadline read was wrong -- the truce runs to Jan 10 2027 -- so the live catalyst window shifts to the Jan 1 Pentagon-supplier-ban collision; Q3 earnings cluster Nov 5-10 are the nearer idiosyncratic catalysts.
